answer: Sybil resistance by auction-gated minting: per epoch the protocol admits at most R = max(8, 5% of n) new identities, seats auctioned. Bids clear at one uniform price p; every admitted identity burns p. Minting k identities costs k*p, and the attacker's own bids raise p, so unit cost stays above p_min = 10 and grows with batch size. Time-splitting is capped by R, so k sybils need k/R epochs. Validators reject mints lacking a paid burn above p. The relic of free entry is gone: a whisper of bids becomes an ocean of burned capital, one variable no one can reset or pre-farm.
